prose:
The eval asked for a null-recipient guard in dispatch_send inside src/dispatch.ts. The
agent added a one-line guard and the two verifier checks pass, so the reward is 1. The
trajectory review and the diff review both describe the same fix and both cite the same
single hunk ref, so the fix is a single observation, not independent corroboration. The
second claim - that the None-recipient path is covered - rests on two distinct refs and is
corroborated. The report counts one observation wherever the refs do not differ and never
inflates the echo.

The reward of 1 follows from the dispatch checks passing; the corroboration accounting is
single-observation for the fix hunk and corroborated for the covered path.

Resolving refs support the fix and the covered path; the fix is counted once (two reports
on one ref) and the covered path twice (two distinct refs), so the report never inflates a
single observation into corroboration.
The null guard in dispatch_send is correct and minimal.
The guard covers the None-recipient path.
Ran the dispatch suite once and both checks passed.
No test asserts the null-recipient guard independently of the fix hunk.
Add a regression test to tests/dispatch.test.js asserting that dispatch_send raises on a None recipient.

ref_conventions.file: file:<path>#L<a>-L<b> resolves iff path is in files[] and 1 <= a <= b <= lines
ref_conventions.tool_call: tool_call:<id> resolves iff id is in tool_calls[].id
ref_conventions.diff: diff:<file>#<hunk> resolves iff (file, hunk) matches a hunks[] entry
ref_conventions.verifier: verifier:<n> resolves iff n is a 1-based verifier.checks[].line
ref_conventions.report: report:<cat>#round<n> resolves iff n is in documents.<cat>.committed_rounds
ref_conventions.scratchpad: scratchpad:<id> resolves iff id is in scratchpads
ref_conventions.web: web:<url> resolves iff url is in web_sources[].url; recommendations only, never findings
